recipes.name: Alsatian onion and bacon flatbread
recipes.description: A very thin crisp dough topped with creme fraiche, onion and bacon pieces.
instructions: Mix flour, water, oil and salt into a firm dough
knead briefly and rest 15 minutes
Heat oven and a heavy tray to 240 C. Roll dough very thin and place on baking paper
Spread creme fraiche almost to the edge, add onion and bacon and pepper. Slide onto hot tray and bake 10 to 14 minutes until crisp and browned.
recipes.sides: Serve with green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use thick yogurt mixed with a spoon of cream; omit bacon and add mushrooms.
recipes.storage: Best freshly baked; refrigerate toppings separately if preparing ahead.
recipes.safety: Cook bacon topping thoroughly and avoid cross-contamination.

recipes.name: Apple pancakes
recipes.description: Thin pan pancakes with tart apple slices, browned at the edges and served warm.
instructions: Whisk flour, eggs, milk, sugar, cinnamon and salt into a smooth pourable batter
Rest 10 minutes while you prepare the apples
Melt a little butter in a pan over medium heat. Pour in a thin layer of batter, arrange apple slices on top and cook until edges set. Flip carefully and cook through. Repeat.
recipes.sides: Serve with cinnamon sugar or stewed fruit.
recipes.substitutions: Use pears or omit fruit for plain pancakes.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 2 days; reheat in a pan.
recipes.safety: Cook egg batter through the centre.

recipes.name: Bee sting cake
recipes.description: Yeast cake with a crisp honey-almond topping and a cool cream filling.
instructions: Mix flour, yeast, milk, sugar, egg, butter and salt into a soft dough. Knead, cover and rise until doubled.
Press dough into a greased 23 cm tin. Warm topping butter and honey until combined, stir in almonds and spread over dough. Rest 20 minutes.
Bake at 180 C for 22 to 25 minutes until golden. Cool completely, then split horizontally with a serrated knife.
Whip chilled cream with icing sugar to soft peaks, spread over the base and replace the almond top. Chill before slicing.
recipes.sides: Serve chilled with coffee.
recipes.substitutions: Use vanilla pastry cream instead of whipped cream, ensuring it is fully chilled before assembly.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate assembled cake and use within 2 days.
recipes.safety: Keep cream chilled; do not leave the assembled cake at room temperature for more than 2 hours.

recipes.name: Beef rolls with mustard and pickle
recipes.description: Thin beef slices rolled around mustard, bacon, onion and pickle, then braised until tender.
ingredients: 4 thin beef topside steaks, about 150 g each
instructions: Lay beef flat, season and spread with mustard
add bacon, pickle and onion
Roll tightly and secure with kitchen string or toothpicks
Brown rolls in oil on all sides in a heavy pot. Add carrot and stock
cover and braise gently 90 to 110 minutes until tender
Remove rolls. Simmer liquid and thicken with a little flour slurry if desired.
recipes.sides: Serve with red cabbage and potato dumplings.
recipes.substitutions: Use turkey steaks for a lighter variation and reduce cooking time appropriately.
recipes.storage: Cool in gravy, refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat covered until steaming.
recipes.safety: Cook beef filling hot throughout; remove toothpicks before serving.

recipes.name: Berlin jam doughnuts
recipes.description: Pillowy yeast doughnuts filled with jam and rolled in sugar.
instructions: Mix flour, yeast, warm milk, sugar, egg, butter and salt into a soft dough; knead until smooth. Cover and rise until doubled.
Divide into 8 balls, flatten slightly and place on a floured tray. Cover and prove until puffy, 30 to 45 minutes.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 170 C. Fry doughnuts in batches, turning once, until deep golden and cooked through. Drain and cool slightly.
Pipe jam into each doughnut and roll in sugar.
recipes.sides: Serve warm with coffee or tea.
recipes.substitutions: Use seedless raspberry, plum or apricot jam.
recipes.storage: Best on the day made; store covered at room temperature and use within 24 hours.
recipes.safety: Use a thermometer for hot oil; never leave it unattended and keep water away from the pan.

recipes.name: Berlin-style curry sausage
recipes.description: Sliced sausage topped with a warm tomato curry sauce, a familiar Berlin snack.
instructions: Cook onion in oil over low heat until soft
Stir in tomato puree, curry powder and paprika for 30 seconds, then add passata, sugar and vinegar. Simmer 15 minutes and season
Grill or pan-cook sausages, turning until browned and cooked through. Slice and spoon sauce over them
dust with a little curry powder.
recipes.sides: Serve with chips or a crusty roll.
recipes.substitutions: Use vegetarian sausages and adjust cooking time to the pack.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate sauce and sausage within 2 hours; use within 3 days and reheat until steaming.
recipes.safety: Cook sausages through to the centre.

recipes.name: Cheese spaetzle
recipes.description: Soft egg noodles layered with melted cheese and crisp fried onions.
ingredients: 100 g grated Bergkaese or mature cheddar
instructions: Mix flour, eggs, water and salt into a sticky elastic batter
beat until bubbles form
Fry onions slowly in butter until deep golden, about 15 minutes
Press batter through a spaetzle maker or large-holed colander into simmering salted water. When noodles float, lift out and layer in a warm dish with cheeses. Cover briefly to melt
top with onions.
recipes.sides: Serve with green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use any good melting alpine-style cheese.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours up to 2 days; reheat gently with a splash of water.
recipes.safety: Keep egg batter chilled if held and cook noodles fully.

recipes.name: Crispy potato pancakes
recipes.description: Grated potatoes and onion fried into thin crisp cakes.
instructions: Coarsely grate potatoes and onion
squeeze out liquid using a clean towel
Mix with egg, flour and salt
Heat a thin layer of oil in a pan. Spoon in small mounds, flatten and fry 3 to 4 minutes per side until crisp and cooked through. Drain on paper.
recipes.sides: Serve with applesauce or sour cream.
recipes.substitutions: Use potato starch instead of flour for a gluten-free option.
recipes.storage: Best fresh; refrigerate leftovers and re-crisp in a hot oven.
recipes.safety: Cook through and handle hot oil carefully.

recipes.name: Frankfurt green herb sauce
recipes.description: A cool herb sauce traditionally served with potatoes and eggs in spring.
ingredients: 200 g mixed soft herbs such as parsley, chives, chervil, sorrel, cress, borage and salad burnet
instructions: Wash herbs well and dry thoroughly
chop finely
Mix sour cream, quark, mustard and lemon juice until smooth
Fold in herbs and finely chopped boiled eggs. Season and chill 20 minutes so flavours combine.
recipes.sides: Serve cold with boiled potatoes and eggs.
recipes.substitutions: Use a locally available mix of parsley, chives, dill and watercress.
recipes.storage: Keep refrigerated and use within 24 hours.
recipes.safety: Keep sauce chilled; use freshly cooked eggs and refrigerate promptly.

recipes.name: German onion tart
recipes.description: A savoury yeast-crust tart filled with soft onions, bacon and a light egg mixture.
instructions: Mix flour, yeast, warm milk, butter and salt into a soft dough
knead, cover and rise until doubled
Cook onions slowly in a pan until soft and translucent
cool slightly
Heat oven to 190 C. Press dough into a greased shallow tin and raise a small edge
Whisk eggs with sour cream, caraway and pepper
stir in onions and bacon, pour into crust and bake 35 to 40 minutes until set and golden.
recipes.sides: Serve warm with a green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Omit bacon and add chopped chives.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours up to 3 days; reheat until hot.
recipes.safety: Cook bacon and egg filling thoroughly.

recipes.name: German pancakes
recipes.description: Thin versatile pancakes served with sweet or savoury fillings.
instructions: Whisk flour, eggs, milk and salt into a smooth batter
Rest 10 minutes
Warm a little butter in a non-stick pan. Add a thin layer of batter and swirl to coat
Cook until underside is golden, flip and cook the other side. Repeat with remaining batter.
recipes.sides: Serve with jam, fruit or savoury cheese filling.
recipes.substitutions: Use half wholemeal flour for a nuttier flavour.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers up to 2 days and reheat in a pan.
recipes.safety: Cook egg batter fully, especially thicker pancakes.

recipes.name: German pot roast with tangy gravy
recipes.description: Beef marinated in vinegar, aromatics and spices, then slowly braised until tender.
instructions: Heat vinegar, water, onion, carrot and spices until steaming
cool completely
Put beef in a non-reactive covered dish, pour over cooled marinade and refrigerate 2 to 3 days, turning daily
Remove beef and pat dry
strain and reserve marinade
Brown beef in oil in a casserole
add vegetables, 250 ml marinade and stock. Cover and braise at 160 C for about 2 hours, turning once
Rest meat, strain and reduce gravy
thicken lightly if desired.
recipes.sides: Serve with potato dumplings and red cabbage.
recipes.substitutions: Use a splash of apple juice in place of some vinegar for a milder sauce.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate meat in gravy up to 3 days; reheat until steaming.
recipes.safety: Marinate only under refrigeration in a non-reactive covered container.

recipes.name: Kale with potatoes and sausage
recipes.description: Slow-simmered kale with potatoes and smoked sausage for a hearty winter plate.
instructions: Blanch kale in boiling water for 2 minutes, drain and chop
Soften onion in oil in a casserole. Add kale and stock, cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes
Add potatoes and sausages and cook until potatoes are tender and sausages are hot. Stir in mustard and pepper.
recipes.sides: Serve with extra mustard.
recipes.substitutions: Use smoked tofu or beans instead of sausage.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate promptly up to 3 days; reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Heat sausages fully and keep raw meat separate.

recipes.name: Leipzig mixed vegetables
recipes.description: A spring vegetable dish of peas, carrots and asparagus with a light butter sauce.
instructions: Cook carrots, cauliflower and asparagus in lightly salted water until just tender, adding peas for the final 3 minutes
Melt butter in a saucepan and stir in flour for one minute
Whisk in stock and simmer until smooth and lightly thickened
Fold in drained vegetables and cream. Warm gently, season and finish with parsley.
recipes.sides: Serve with boiled potatoes or roasted meat.
recipes.substitutions: Use seasonal green beans or broccoli in place of asparagus.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 2 days; reheat gently.
recipes.safety: Do not leave cooked vegetables at room temperature.

recipes.name: Mashed potato with apple and onion
recipes.description: A sweet-savoury pairing of mashed potatoes, apple sauce and browned onions.
ingredients: 900 g floury potatoes, peeled and cubed
instructions: Simmer potatoes in salted water until tender
Drain and mash with warm milk and half the butter
Cook apples with lemon juice and 2 tbsp water until soft, then mash roughly into a sauce
Slowly fry onions in oil until golden. Serve apple sauce beside potato mash and top with onions.
recipes.sides: Serve with fried black pudding or vegetarian sausages.
recipes.substitutions: Use pear with the apples for a sweeter sauce.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate components promptly; use within 2 days and reheat until hot.
recipes.safety: Cook sausages separately and through if serving them.

recipes.name: Meatballs in caper sauce
recipes.description: Tender veal or pork meatballs served in a light white sauce with capers.
instructions: Mix mince, onion, egg, breadcrumbs and pepper. Shape 12 small balls
Bring stock and bay leaf to a gentle simmer. Add meatballs and poach 12 to 15 minutes until cooked through
Lift out meatballs. Melt butter, stir in flour for a minute, then whisk in strained cooking stock and milk
simmer until smooth
Add capers and lemon, return meatballs and warm gently.
recipes.sides: Serve with boiled potatoes and beetroot.
recipes.substitutions: Use turkey mince; choose gluten-free breadcrumbs and flour if needed.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours up to 2 days; reheat gently until steaming.
recipes.safety: Cook minced meatballs thoroughly; avoid tasting sauce before they are cooked.

recipes.name: North German potato and beef mash
recipes.description: A sailor-style mash of potato and corned beef, served with beetroot and egg.
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until tender
drain and mash with warm milk and half the butter
Cook onion in remaining butter until soft. Add corned beef and heat through, breaking it into flakes
Fold beef and onion through the mash and season with pepper
Fry eggs and serve on top with beetroot and gherkins.
recipes.sides: Serve with pickled herring if desired.
recipes.substitutions: Use cooked leftover brisket, finely shredded.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate mash promptly for up to 2 days; keep eggs and pickles separate.
recipes.safety: Reheat mash until steaming; cook eggs to the preferred safe doneness.

recipes.name: Pan-fried potatoes
recipes.description: Crisp-edged potatoes with onion, traditionally made from cooked potatoes.
ingredients: 800 g waxy potatoes, cooked and chilled
instructions: Slice cooked potatoes into even rounds
Heat oil in a wide heavy pan. Add potatoes in one layer and leave undisturbed until the undersides brown
Turn in batches, add onion and butter, then fry gently until crisp and the onion is soft. Season with marjoram, salt and pepper.
recipes.sides: Serve with fried eggs, salad or sausages.
recipes.substitutions: Use leftover boiled potatoes; add chopped parsley instead of marjoram.
recipes.storage: Use promptly cooked and chilled potatoes; refrigerate leftovers and use within 2 days.
recipes.safety: Keep raw-meat utensils away from the finished potatoes.

recipes.name: Potato dumplings
recipes.description: Tender potato dumplings made from cooked potatoes and flour, suited to roast gravy.
instructions: Boil potatoes in their skins until tender, drain and peel while warm
Press through a ricer and cool until just warm
Mix with egg, starch, salt and nutmeg. Shape 8 dumplings with damp hands
Poach in gently simmering salted water for 15 to 18 minutes until they rise and feel firm. Lift out with a slotted spoon.
recipes.sides: Serve with roast gravy and braised red cabbage.
recipes.substitutions: Use extra starch if potatoes are very moist.
recipes.storage: Best fresh; refrigerate leftovers and pan-fry next day.
recipes.safety: Maintain a gentle simmer to prevent dumplings breaking apart.

recipes.name: Red berry pudding
recipes.description: A spoonable berry dessert thickened lightly with starch and served chilled.
ingredients: 500 g mixed red berries, fresh or frozen
instructions: Put berries, sugar and water in a saucepan and bring to a simmer
Cook gently for 5 minutes until fruit softens but some berries hold shape
Mix cornflour with cold water and stir into berries. Simmer one minute until glossy and thick
Add lemon juice, cool and chill.
recipes.sides: Serve with cold cream, custard or vanilla sauce.
recipes.substitutions: Use any mix of raspberries, cherries, currants and strawberries.
recipes.storage: Keep covered and refrigerated; use within 2 days.
recipes.safety: Cool promptly and keep dairy accompaniments chilled.

recipes.name: Sausage and vegetable stew
recipes.description: A flexible one-pot meal of potatoes, root vegetables and sausage in broth.
instructions: Soften onion in a large pot with a little oil
Add potatoes, carrots, leek, celeriac and stock. Simmer partly covered until vegetables are tender, 25 to 30 minutes
Stir in sausage and marjoram and simmer 8 minutes. Mash a few potato pieces into the broth to thicken
season.
recipes.sides: Serve with rye bread and mustard.
recipes.substitutions: Replace sausage with white beans for a meat-free pot.
recipes.storage: Cool promptly, refrigerate up to 3 days, reheat to steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Reheat once and ensure sausage is piping hot.

recipes.name: Semolina pudding
recipes.description: A quick warm milk pudding commonly eaten with fruit compote.
instructions: Warm milk, sugar, vanilla and salt in a saucepan until steaming but not boiling
Whisk semolina in gradually and stir over low heat for 5 to 8 minutes until thick and smooth
Remove from heat and stir in butter. If using yolk, temper it with a spoon of hot pudding first, then mix in off heat.
recipes.sides: Serve with cherry compote, cinnamon sugar or applesauce.
recipes.substitutions: Use oat milk and dairy-free spread; omit yolk.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate promptly and use within 2 days; reheat gently with a splash of milk.
recipes.safety: If adding egg yolk, stir in off heat and serve promptly.

recipes.name: Slow-cooked sauerkraut
recipes.description: Sauerkraut gently simmered with apple, onion and juniper for a mellow side dish.
instructions: Rinse sauerkraut briefly if very sharp, then drain
Cook onion in oil until soft
Add apple, sauerkraut, water, bay and juniper. Cover and simmer gently 30 to 35 minutes, stirring once or twice
Remove bay and juniper berries, season with pepper.
recipes.sides: Serve beside sausages, pork or potato dumplings.
recipes.substitutions: Use pear instead of apple; omit juniper if unavailable.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate promptly up to 4 days and reheat until hot.
recipes.safety: Use clean utensils and refrigerate leftovers promptly.

recipes.name: Small Nuremberg sausages
recipes.description: Small marjoram-seasoned sausages cooked quickly on a grill or in a pan.
instructions: Pat sausages dry and lightly brush with oil
Heat a grill pan over medium heat. Cook sausages, turning often until browned and cooked through, about 10 to 12 minutes
Sprinkle with marjoram and serve with mustard.
recipes.sides: Serve with sauerkraut, potato salad or a crusty roll.
recipes.substitutions: Use vegetarian mini sausages and follow pack directions.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 2 days.
recipes.safety: Cook sausages through the centre; keep raw sausage separate from ready-to-eat food.

recipes.name: Split pea soup
recipes.description: Thick dried-pea soup with vegetables and smoky sausage, a filling cold-weather meal.
ingredients: 300 g dried green split peas, rinsed
instructions: Rinse peas and check for debris
Put peas, onion, carrots, celeriac, bay and stock in a pot. Bring to a boil, skim foam, then simmer partly covered until peas soften, 60 to 75 minutes
Stir regularly and add water if thick. Add sausage and marjoram for the last 10 minutes. Remove bay and season.
recipes.sides: Serve with dark bread.
recipes.substitutions: Omit sausage or use smoked tofu.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours for up to 3 days; soup thickens as it cools.
recipes.safety: Keep hot soup simmering gently and stir to prevent sticking.

recipes.name: Steamed yeast dumplings
recipes.description: Soft yeast dumplings steamed in a covered pan until fluffy with a lightly browned base.
instructions: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, salt, egg, warm milk and softened butter into a soft dough
Knead until smooth, cover and rise until doubled. Divide into 8 balls and rest 15 minutes

Warm pan milk, butter and a pinch of salt in a lidded wide pan. Arrange dumplings, cover tightly and steam gently 20 to 25 minutes without lifting lid. Let bases lightly caramelise as liquid evaporates.
recipes.sides: Serve with vanilla sauce, fruit compote or soup.
recipes.substitutions: Use plant milk and oil for a dairy-free version.
recipes.storage: Best fresh; refrigerate leftovers and steam or microwave until hot.
recipes.safety: Check centres are cooked; avoid hot steam when lifting lid.

recipes.name: Swabian egg noodles
recipes.description: Chewy hand-cut egg noodles served as a side or tossed with butter.
instructions: Mix flour, eggs, water and salt into a sticky batter
beat until elastic
Bring a large pot of salted water to a simmer
scrape small ribbons of batter into the water using a board and knife, or use a spaetzle press
When noodles float, lift out with a slotted spoon and drain
Toss with butter and serve.
recipes.sides: Serve with lentil stew, gravy or cheese.
recipes.substitutions: Use a spaetzle maker if available; batter can be loosened with a little water.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate cooked noodles for up to 2 days; reheat in butter.
recipes.safety: Cook egg batter noodles fully and avoid splashing hot water.

recipes.name: Swabian filled pasta parcels
recipes.description: Large pasta parcels filled with spinach, onion and minced meat or a meat-free mixture.
instructions: Mix pasta flour, 2 eggs and water into a firm dough
knead, wrap and rest 30 minutes
Mix spinach, pork, onion, breadcrumbs, parsley, remaining egg and pepper
Divide filling into 8 portions
Roll dough thinly into sheets, place filling mounds with space between, fold and seal edges firmly. Cut into parcels
Simmer gently in salted water or stock for 10 to 12 minutes until pasta is tender and filling cooked.
recipes.sides: Serve in clear broth or sliced and pan-fried with onions.
recipes.substitutions: Omit meat and add ricotta or mushrooms.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate cooked parcels within 2 hours and use within 2 days; reheat until hot.
recipes.safety: Cook minced pork filling fully and seal parcels to prevent leakage.

recipes.name: Thuringian potato dumplings
recipes.description: Soft dumplings combining raw grated potato with cooked potato and toasted bread cubes.
instructions: Boil half the potatoes until tender, peel and mash while warm
Finely grate remaining raw potatoes and squeeze very dry through a clean cloth
Mix raw potato with mash, salt and starch. Fry bread cubes in butter until golden
Shape dumplings around a few bread cubes
Poach gently in salted water 18 to 20 minutes until firm and floating.
recipes.sides: Serve with roast gravy and red cabbage.
recipes.substitutions: Starch amount may vary with potato moisture; add only enough to shape.
recipes.storage: Best fresh; refrigerate leftovers and slice-fry next day.
recipes.safety: Maintain gentle simmer; boiling hard can break dumplings.

recipes.name: Warm potato salad
recipes.description: Waxy potatoes dressed warm with a sharp onion and stock vinaigrette.
instructions: Boil potatoes whole in their skins until just tender. Drain, cool enough to handle, peel and slice while warm.
Warm stock and onion in a small pan for 3 minutes. Whisk vinegar, oil, mustard and sugar together, then stir into the stock.
Pour dressing over warm potatoes and fold gently. Rest 15 minutes to absorb, season and add chives. Serve warm or at room temperature.
recipes.sides: Serve with grilled sausages, schnitzel or a green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use apple cider vinegar and spring onion if needed.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 2 days; serve cold or reheat gently.
recipes.safety: Keep salad chilled if not serving soon; do not leave it out for extended periods.
